That precise location corresponds to the pes anserinus insertion (conjoined tendons of sartorius, gracilis, semitendinosus) and the overlying pes anserine bursa. Obesity and new repetitive valgus/pivoting stresses are known risk factors for pes anserine bursitis/tendinopathy. Examination shows no joint effusion, full ROM, negative ligament tests, and no systemic signs of infection—findings that make intra-articular pathology (meniscal tear, ligament rupture), prepatellar bursitis, septic bursitis, or patellar tendinopathy less likely. X-ray is normal, which argues against fracture or bony avulsion (and Osgood–Schlatter is unlikely given age). Taken together, the history, anatomic location of maximal tenderness, risk factors, and negative intra-articular exam findings most strongly support pes anserine bursitis/tendinopathy.

DIAGNOSIS: Pes anserine (anserine) bursitis / pes anserinus tendinopathy
